title: When waiting is long
tomorrow: a phone rings at 2 a.m. what do you say on the drive?

cards: A waitlist that says forty-first, and the next morning, still forty-first. A hospital room where nothing changes but the nurses. Some waits come with no date on them.
The Qur'an tells of a father with no date either. Ya'qub's sons come home without their brother Yusuf, carrying his shirt with false blood on it.
Ya'qub looks at the shirt, doesn't believe a word, and says something he'll have to say again, much later.

teach.b: In Pickthall's words: "(My course is) comely patience." In Arabic, sabr jamil: beautiful patience. Later, when more sons are lost to him, he says it again.
And then, his eyes whitened with grief, he says: "I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah." So beautiful patience isn't a dry face. He wept.
What makes it beautiful is where the complaint goes: to God, not against Him. And he doesn't just sit.
He sends his sons out to search, and tells them not to despair of the Spirit of Allah. And the surah doesn't leave him there.
It ends with another shirt, Yusuf's own, carried home and laid on his father's face, and his sight comes back.

teach.h: A SHIRT OPENS IT, A SHIRT CLOSES IT.
teach.b: A shirt opened the waiting, and a shirt closes it. Now look back over this week of hard days. Troubled by it means faith.
Weep, and trust. Seek the cure.
Never alone. Not if only. The best return.
Every one of them is a way of waiting well: honest with God, tender with yourself, still looking for the door.

how: Muslims often recall Ya'qub's words, sabr jamil, in long trials, and turn to du'a, telling God their grief while continuing to act; Surah Yusuf is read for comfort in hard seasons.

games.q: what does “when waiting is long” mean?
o: a wait you're meant to endure without feeling
a long wait that proves God has forgotten you
a long wait carried with beautiful patience and hope

games.q: the week's hard days — tap the pairs.
p: Ya'qub's answer to the bloody shirt
the Prophet on his own tears

s: beautiful patience means Ya'qub never cried
his eyes whitened with grief; he took his distress to Allah.
Ya'qub sent his sons to search and told them not to despair
despair not of the Spirit of Allah, he said.
the hadith on doubt calls the doubting thought itself faith
the Prophet called the companions' distress at the thought clear faith.

games.q: a friend has waited months for a visa interview and says 'patience means i shouldn't even ask about it anymore.' what does Ya'qub's story suggest?
o: beautiful patience still asks and searches; it just takes its grief to God.
patience means silence; asking again would show weak faith.
patience is for small things; with big ones it's fine to despair.
games.why: Ya'qub wept, told Allah his anguish, and sent his sons to search. beautiful patience isn't passive.

practice: Find one slow, steady sound: a clock, the fridge, rain, or your own breath if the room is silent. Listen to it the way someone listens while waiting for a door to open, without hurrying it.
If you pray, let the waiting you carry go to Allah, the way Ya'qub took his; if not, just let the sound keep time.

wordCard.voice: When waiting is long: Ya'qub's answer, sabr jamil. The grief goes to God, and the search goes on.

orig.note: Arabic: beautiful patience, Ya'qub's words (12:18); Pickthall: 'comely patience'.

carryVoice: Your line: beautiful patience. It weeps, and it keeps looking for the door. Until next time.
